title: Pack each product in the smallest carton it fits
instruction: Pack each product into the smallest carton it fits in, one product per carton.
context: E-commerce and warehouse packing: choosing the smallest carton that holds an item cuts void fill and dimensional-weight shipping costs. Unlike fitting a part to its one matching hole, a larger carton also accepts the item; the packer must judge which fitting carton is smallest.
setup: A wooden table; all positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. Three open-top cardboard cartons (6 mm walls, 25 mm deep, no lids) stand open side up in a row 360 mm forward: a small carton (inner 45 x 50 mm, front to back x side to side) centered 120 mm toward the left arm, a medium carton (inner 55 x 70 mm) centered 18 mm toward the left arm, and a large carton (inner 65 x 85 mm) centered 101.5 mm toward the right arm. Two rigid products lie flat on the table 220 mm forward: a blue box (42 x 58 x 30 mm, 60 g) 140 mm toward the left arm, and an orange box (52 x 74 x 30 mm, 80 g) 120 mm toward the right arm, each with its longer side running side to side.
scoring: Per product: 0.5 if it lies flat on the floor of the smallest carton it fits in (blue: medium carton; orange: large carton), with its center inside that carton's opening; 0.2 if it lies flat inside a larger carton instead; 0 if it is anywhere else, propped on a rim, tilted or still held. The score is the sum (1.0 at most). Success (1.0) once both are in their smallest cartons and still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lift the products out and return them to their start positions (tape marks); the cartons are taped to the table.
fidelity: Rigid boxes for the products and carton walls; cartons are fixed to the table, with no flaps or lids. Lying flat means the product's center is within 4 mm of its resting height on the carton floor. The blue product does not fit the small carton (58 vs 50 mm) nor the orange one the medium carton (74 vs 70 mm), in any orientation.
